text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, "Liberation Mono", monospace

svg.text: On the right: the runs that start each day, the runner-hours used each day, and their share of the ASF daily budget, i.e. the weekly limit of 25 runners x 24h = 600 runner-
hours. The bottom row shows the peak of each hour and the daily averages.
Bars start at the cron time and last for the estimated duration. Their thickness and the 'x N' in their labels show the estimated average number of runners a run keeps busy.
Both estimates are medians of recent apache/spark runs, in ESTIMATES of dev/visualize_ci_schedule.py; runs can take longer, use more runners at their busiest, or start late.
Branch builds are dispatched by the branch*_scheduler.yml workflows through dev/dispatch-if-changed.sh, which skips a run when the branch has not changed since its last
successful run, so the real load on maintenance branches is usually lower.
Workflows scheduled directly run on master. When this SVG is opened on its own, hovering over a bar shows its cron entry and the file that defines it.
Not shown because they usually finish within an hour and do not run tests: build_infra_images_cache.yml ('0 4 * * *', refreshes the CI image cache); labeler.yml ('7-59/10 * *
* *', labels PRs); pages.yml ('30 12 * * *', deploys the documentation site); stale.yml ('30 4 * * *', closes stale PRs); update_build_status.yml ('*/10 * * * *', syncs PR
build status); update_build_status.yml ('35 2-22/4 * * *', syncs PR build status).
ASF limits apache/spark to 25 full-time runners on average per calendar week and 30 over any five consecutive days, for all of its workflows including the builds of pushes,
and to 20 concurrent jobs per workflow; see https://infra.apache.org/github-actions-policy.html and .github/workflows/README.md for the scheduling guidelines.
